maintainer: Tianyang Liu, Canwen Xu, Julian McAuley
measures: Repository-level code auto-completion in Python and Java through retrieval (RepoBench-R), next-line completion (RepoBench-C), and a retrieval-plus-completion pipeline (RepoBench-P); the released evaluator reports exact match, edit similarity, and CodeBLEU.
notes: The official repository documents v1.1, cross-file-first/cross-file-random/in-file settings, and public Hugging Face datasets. It is a strong repository-context signal but not a whole-repository repair benchmark.

measures: Architecture-aware repository comprehension: 500 open-ended questions from GitHub Discussions over 50 repositories and 15 languages, graded with weighted checklist verification across project architecture, business logic, and implementation details.
notes: The repository README states that current results are tied to the paper's scaffold and that scores are comparable only under the same agent scaffolding/tool budget. Model ids and values are copied from the public README; they are not current working-ladder ids.

maintainer: XLang Lab (verified-leaderboard maintainers named on the site)
measures: 369 real computer tasks (361 excluding Google Drive tasks) involving real web and desktop apps, OS file I/O and cross-application workflows on Windows/macOS/Ubuntu; multimodal agents, execution-verified
notes: Verified-leaderboard rows (BenchLM OSWorld-Verified, Sep 22 2026; the official verified leaderboard requires a maintainer-run session). OSWorld 2.0 is a newer, harder variant with separate scores: vendor-reported coverage puts Gemini 3.8 Flash at 59.0% and Claude Opus 5 at ~75.4% on OSWorld-2.0 (Google's table as quoted by third parties); scores are not comparable across variants. steel.dev tracks 21 OSWorld and 22 OSWorld 2.0 sourced results. Dimension D-DEBUG per the launch enum corresponds to F-02 D-TERM (terminal/autonomous execution). Contamination risk low: dynamic real environments with execution-based verification.

measures: Tool-agent-user interaction in realistic domains (retail, airline, telecom, banking, knowledge): dual-control simulation where agent and (simulated) user both act on a shared world state; average pass rate across domains
notes: GLM-5.2 99.1% is the highest published tau2 score (BenchLM compiled ledger, 151 models) but BenchLM itself warns the available coverage and evaluation setups do not establish comparability; pricepertoken lists the same 99.1% (Aug 16 2026). Gemini 3.7 Flash 80.6% is the OpenRouter tau2-Bench Airline leaderboard leader (snapshot 2026-09-27). Mistral Medium 3.5 94.2% is an aggregator figure (requesty.ai); Mistral's own model card claims 91.4% on the newer tau3-Telecom instead. tau2-bench v1.0.1 (July 2026) fixed banking_knowledge grading: results before and after are not comparable. tau3 exists; tau-bench.com hosts the official leaderboard. Dimension D-DEBUG (launch enum) corresponds to F-02 D-TERM autonomous execution.

measures: Code editing correctness and edit-format compliance on 225 difficult Exercism exercises across C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, and Rust.

scores.score: Percent completed correctly=61.7%; percent using correct edit format=91.5%
Percent completed correctly=45.3%; percent using correct edit format=100.0%
Percent completed correctly=8.0%; percent using correct edit format=71.6%

notes: This is a dated benchmark snapshot: the page says it was designed to spread frontier scores across a roughly 5%-50% range and reports the exact model labels shown. Scores are Aider's published snapshot, not a fresh independent reproduction.

measures: Coding-challenge competence across programming problems evaluated with executable tests; the public repository provides training and evaluation code and the APPS dataset.
notes: The official repository identifies the benchmark paper, dataset download, and Hugging Face dataset. The corpus is public and fixed; no contamination rate is asserted by the source, so the risk label is a collector classification.

measures: Function-level code generation for 1,140 practical software-engineering-oriented tasks with complex instructions and diverse function calls; includes Instruct/Complete settings and a 148-task BigCodeBench-Hard subset evaluated by execution and pass@k.
notes: The official repository links the paper, dataset, evaluator, and live Hugging Face leaderboard and states that many models have been evaluated. No exact score for a current working-ladder model was recorded from the accessed primary text.

measures: Competition-level code generation on recent Codeforces problems, with direct submission and an Elo calculation intended to be comparable with human ratings and percentiles.
notes: The repository and paper state that CodeElo compiles the recent six months of Codeforces problems and reports 30 open-source plus three proprietary model Elo ratings. Scores are paper-reported and are not current working-ladder ids.

measures: Live competitive-programming problems judged by the Codeforces platform, including executable submissions, contest divisions, and human participant ratings.
notes: Codeforces is a live platform rather than one frozen LLM benchmark. CodeElo uses recent Codeforces contest problems and direct platform submissions; public problem statements still create exposure after release.

measures: Efficiency of LLM-generated code on performance-exercising coding tasks and test inputs, complementing functional correctness with execution-efficiency evaluation.
notes: EvalPlus README links EvalPerf to its COLM 2024 paper and documentation. No score is recorded here because the accessed primary source did not provide a score for a current working-ladder model.

measures: Stricter execution-based code-correctness evaluation: HumanEval+ adds substantially more tests to HumanEval and MBPP+ adds substantially more tests to MBPP; the leaderboard reports greedy pass@1 before and after the stronger tests.
notes: The project README documents the datasets, leaderboard, EvalPerf extension, and a contamination warning that model providers must avoid contaminated data. Scores are benchmark-maintainer leaderboard values; ids are copied verbatim from results.json.

measures: Function-level Python code generation evaluated by executing generated completions against unit tests; reports pass@k.
notes: Primary repository describes the HumanEval harness and execution-based pass@1/pass@10/pass@100. The score source is the EvalPlus maintainer leaderboard, not an independent reproduction; model ids are copied verbatim. Risk is a collector classification for a public fixed 2021 corpus, not a measured contamination rate.

measures: HumanEval-derived code-generation evaluation across three scenarios and six programming languages, using translated tasks and executable evaluation.
notes: The BigCode evaluation harness lists HumanEvalPack as extending HumanEval to three scenarios across six languages and links the public dataset. No current working-ladder score was found in the accessed source.

maintainer: LiveCodeBench team (paper: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code)
measures: Competitive programming (LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces) collected continuously over time windows; code generation; designed contamination-free with delayed public release
notes: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max 93.5 Pass@1 is a vendor claim from the April 2026 launch (morphllm flags it as vendor-run); llm-stats lists it as leader at 0.935 across 75 models. Contamination risk low by design (time-windowed collection, delayed public release per BenchLM). Dimension: the F-02 frame names this skill D-ALGO (algorithmic coding); the launch enum has no D-ALGO, so it is recorded as D-IMPL. Multiple dataset versions exist (Kaggle notes versioning), so rows are comparable only within a version.

measures: Around 1,000 crowd-sourced Python programming problems with a task description, reference solution, and automated tests; the repository defines train/validation/test task-id partitions and a hand-verified sanitized subset.
notes: The official Google Research README states the corpus size, task structure, sanitized subset, and split ids. Scores are from the public EvalPlus leaderboard and are not current working-ladder model ids. Risk is a collector classification for a long-public fixed corpus.

measures: Multilingual code-generation evaluation by translating HumanEval-style tasks into 18 programming languages and executing generated programs.
notes: The BigCode evaluation harness identifies MultiPL-E as an evaluation suite based on HumanEval translated into 18 languages. Public translated tasks imply contamination exposure; no measured contamination rate was found.

measures: 300-task subset of SWE-bench Full; same issue-resolving task, lighter eval cost
notes: Same construction and exposure as SWE-bench Full/Verified, hence contamination risk high. Fewer ladder-model rows were found for Lite than for Verified in this pass; ladder models without a public Lite row stay unknown. Largely superseded by Verified in 2026 reporting.

measures: Resolving 300 curated real-world GitHub pull-request tasks across 42 repositories in 9 programming languages (C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, PHP, Ruby, Rust)
notes: Claude Opus 5.5 93.9% appears in llm-stats comparison tables (Anthropic system-card figures). Claude Mythos Preview 0.873 leads the llm-stats aggregate (34 models). Harder than SWE-bench Verified with a wider performance spread (launch discussion on r/LocalLLaMA). Public PR-derived tasks - contamination risk high.

maintainer: SWE-bench team (integrated into the SWE-bench repository Jan 13 2025)
measures: SWE-bench issue resolution with visual context (screenshots, design mockups) added to issue descriptions
notes: Very thin coverage: llm-stats lists 5 evaluated models, all self-reported; BenchLM lists 4 (display-only, excluded from its rankings). Claude Opus 5.5 0.614 is the llm-stats leader. Contamination risk high by construction (public repos plus public visual artifacts).

measures: Larger contamination-resistant SWE benchmark from more recent tasks, run on Scale's standardized SEAL harness; public and private (held-out) subsets
notes: Claude Opus 5.5 0.899 leads the llm-stats aggregate (59 models); Claude Opus 4.8 69.2% and Gemini 3.8 Flash 61.6% are vendor-run figures (morphllm keeps a SEAL-dagger distinction; DataCamp quotes Google's announcement table), while Muse Spark 1.1 61.5% is the top score on Scale's standardized SEAL board (Aug 2026). The vendor-vs-standardized gap is the largest of any benchmark in this catalog. Contamination risk low: Scale's positioning is contamination resistance, plus a held-out private subset.

maintainer: SWE-bench team (Jimenez et al.); Verified is the 500-task human-reviewed subset co-released with OpenAI researchers
measures: Resolving real GitHub issues in Python repositories: model writes a patch that must pass the issue's fail-to-pass tests; the most-cited coding-agent benchmark
notes: Vendor claims marked per source: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max 80.6% is DeepSeek's own April 2026 launch number (morphllm coverage); Mistral Medium 3.5 77.6% is Mistral's model-card claim (mirrored on ollama.com). Claude Opus 5 has no Anthropic-reported SWE-bench number (morphllm); the 97.00% is a Vals.ai run tracked by steel.dev. Contamination risk high: tasks come from public pre-cutoff GitHub issues, and Scale AI positions its newer SWE-bench Pro as the contamination-resistant alternative; vendor-scaffold numbers routinely exceed standardized-harness numbers by wide margins (Fable 5 ~80% vendor vs Muse Spark 1.1 61.5% top on Scale SEAL).

maintainer: OpenAI (benchmark data, automated grading workflow, public leaderboard via GitHub Pages)
measures: 1,400+ real freelance software engineering tasks from Upwork valued at $1M USD in real payouts; both IC coding tasks and manager tasks, scored by end-to-end tests and payout value
notes: Very thin third-party coverage: llm-stats lists 4 models on the full benchmark, all self-reported. GPT-5 1.000 is on the IC-Diamond subset only (6 models). F-02 names SWE-Lancer Manager as the sole public D-CRIT (adversarial review) proxy, at most WEAK; the IC subset maps to D-IMPL. Contamination risk unknown: tasks are real past Upwork jobs published in the repository, but no contamination study was found in this pass (contamination studies are collector B's scope).

measures: Repository-level automatic code review on 200 real pull requests from 50 active open-source projects across 10 languages, preserving full repository context; evaluates issue positioning, issue classification, context understanding, precision, recall, line precision, and noise rate.
notes: The repository describes AI-assisted, expert-verified annotations and links the paper and Hugging Face dataset. Public PRs and comments create exposure, but the source does not publish a measured contamination rate.

measures: Code-review-agent evaluation on pull requests using tests generated from human reviews as a held-out quality gate; measures whether generated review findings match review-relevant behavior rather than only judging prose similarity.
notes: The primary paper abstract states that the benchmark evaluates open-source and commercial review agents including PR-agent, Devin, Claude Code, and Codex, and reports only an aggregate statement that the agents together solve around 40% of tasks. No individual score or repository maintainer was verified from the accessed public source.

measures: Context-rich, fine-grained code review across hunk-level quality assessment, line-level defect localization, and line-level comment generation; the paper describes 67,910 context-enriched entries derived from 153.7K issues and pull requests.
notes: The public paper identifies the dataset and repository and reports that it was deployed at ByteDance. The repository identity was reachable but did not expose a maintainer name in the accessed metadata.

measures: Review-quality evaluation using over 15,000 submissions from four academic venues, reviewer/submission features, LLM judgments, and a human-annotated subset of more than 700 paper-review pairs across 13 quality dimensions.
notes: The repository provides reproducible code and links the paper, Hugging Face dataset, and human annotations. It is a review-quality benchmark, not a code-diff defect-detection benchmark; no current working-ladder score was found.

measures: Execution-based secure code generation on 255 Python tasks across 77 CWE categories, with paired insecure/secure implementations and functional plus vulnerability-targeted security tests; supports Pass@k and security-aware variants.
notes: The public repository identifies the ISSTA 2026 paper and the released Hugging Face dataset. The source says the baseline/full experimental code is still being organized, so benchmark availability and harness completeness should be tracked separately.

measures: Outcome-driven joint evaluation of functional correctness and security on the same generated programs, using executable task oracles and security checks rather than treating passing functional tests as sufficient.
notes: The public repository provides a Dockerized evaluator, model-generation examples, and isolated evaluation guidance for insecure code. No score is recorded because the accessed primary README exposed commands/model ids but not a numeric result table.

measures: Interactive cybersecurity-agent evaluation on 40 professional-level CTF tasks from four competitions, with end-to-end success, subtask-guided success, subtask progress, and first-solve-time measures in a Kali-based environment.

scores.score: End-to-End % Solved=12.5 (n=40); Subtask-Guided % Solved=17.5; Subtasks % Solved=28.7

notes: The public leaderboard aggregates benchmark runs and model/system-card results; superscript footnote markers are retained exactly as written in the CSV. The page warns that one HAL/Inspect port likely leaked an answer for a task and says the OpenAI o3-mini/o1-mini scores were adjusted downward; this is a concrete integrity concern, not a measured training-data contamination rate.

measures: Security evaluation for coding assistants covering insecure-code generation and compliance when asked to assist cyberattacks, with automated test-case generation and evaluation pipelines.
notes: The primary paper describes a unified cybersecurity benchmark and a case study across seven models from Llama 2, Code Llama, and OpenAI GPT families. No per-model score was copied because the accessed abstract does not give one.

measures: Cybersecurity risk and capability evaluation adding prompt-injection, code-interpreter-abuse, cyberattack-helpfulness, and exploit-generation test sets, including a false-refusal-rate utility measure.
notes: The primary paper reports evaluation of GPT-4, Mistral, Meta Llama 3 70B-Instruct, and Code Llama and states a 26%-41% successful-prompt-injection range across tested models, but does not map each endpoint to an exact model score in the accessed abstract, so no score object is invented.

measures: Eight cybersecurity risk/capability evaluations across risks to third parties and to application developers/end users, adding automated social engineering, scaled manual offensive cyber operations, and autonomous offensive cyber operations.
notes: The paper is the public successor release to CyberSecEval and discusses applying the suite to Llama 3 and contemporaneous state-of-the-art models. No per-model score is recorded from the accessed abstract.

measures: Scanner and LLM vulnerability detection on 26 intentionally vulnerable Python repositories with 796 hand-labeled entries, including 676 vulnerabilities and 120 false-positive traps; reports F1 and recall-weighted F3.
notes: The primary abstract calls RealVuln a versioned, community-driven living benchmark and reports a scanner comparison. The score is paper-reported; this is vulnerability detection on repositories, not secure code generation.

maintainer: Tencent Zhuque Lab / Tencent Security Keen Lab / Tsinghua University / HKPolyU / OpenCompass collaborators
measures: Multidimensional cybersecurity evaluation with 44,823 multiple-choice and 3,087 short-answer questions, covering knowledge retention and logical reasoning in Chinese and English across nine cybersecurity domains.
notes: The repository links the paper, Hugging Face dataset, and Zenodo artifact and states that 16 SOTA LLMs were benchmarked, but the accessed README did not expose per-model numeric scores. It is security knowledge/reasoning rather than secure code generation.

maintainer: TQRG / Sofia Reis and Rui Abreu
measures: Security-oriented code-repair data mined from GitHub: the repository states 676 real security vulnerabilities from 114 projects, with vulnerable and fixing commits, CWE classification, and CVE severity where available.
notes: The official repository describes the 2020 update and says a new version is being worked on. This is a vulnerability-patch corpus rather than a ready-made frontier-model leaderboard.

maintainer: S2E Lab / Mohammed Latif Siddiq and Joanna C. S. Santos
measures: Secure-code-generation evaluation using prompts mapped to CWEs; the current repository release states 121 prompts covering 69 CWEs and provides vulnerable examples, generated-code artifacts, and CodeQL/Bandit/manual evaluation paths.
notes: The repository states that v2.1 updated the dataset while preserving old model results and that the original release contained 130 samples for 75 vulnerability types. It is a fixed public security corpus; no contamination rate was found.

maintainer: Mathematical Association of America (competition); benchmark usage and leaderboards are community/aggregator-maintained
measures: 30 integer-answer olympiad mathematics problems (two 15-problem sittings) from the 2025 American Invitational Mathematics Examination; pass@1
notes: Status stale: a fixed February 2025 exam, saturated at the top (multiple leaders at 100%) and superseded by harder math benchmarks (sources note reasoning-model saturation of AIME-class benchmarks; Epoch AI tracks FrontierMath tiers as successors). Contamination risk high: the problems have been public since early 2025 and are widely present in training corpora. No ladder-specific Opus 5.5 / Gemini 3.8 / Mistral Medium 3.5 AIME 2025 row was found in this pass - unknown, not invented.

measures: Abstract visual reasoning on novel grid puzzles (ARC core); fluid intelligence and skill acquisition; reported with a cost-per-task efficiency metric
notes: Semi-Private scores, all verified runs on the official ARC Prize leaderboard (v1 column). v1 is saturated at the top and superseded by ARC-AGI-2/3 - status stale. Contamination risk high: the public training set has been available for years, and the ARC-AGI 3 paper (as reported in community discussion of the leaderboard) alleges frontier models, including Gemini 3, memorized tasks similar to v1/v2; treat as an allegation, not a finding. Model strings recorded exactly as the leaderboard writes them (effort in parentheses).

measures: Next-generation abstract reasoning: harder novel grid puzzles stressing state-of-the-art reasoning, with human calibration (400+ participants) and a cost efficiency metric
notes: Semi-Private verified scores from the official leaderboard (v2 column), except Claude Opus 5 90.4% from its ARC Prize results page (Max reasoning effort). Per-model result pages exist, e.g. https://arcprize.org/results/anthropic-claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5: 91.7% Max, 92.5% XHigh, 93.3% High on v2 Semi-Private). Mistral Medium 3.5 has no ARC-AGI entry on the leaderboard - stays unknown. Contamination medium: semi-private eval set, but the ARC-AGI 3 paper (as reported in community discussion) alleges memorization of similar tasks for v1/v2 scores; allegation, not a finding. llm-stats lists GPT-6 Astra at 0.950 on ARC-AGI v2, consistent with the official 95.0%.

measures: Hardest current ARC generation: novel reasoning tasks where standard-effort runs cost thousands of dollars per task; efficiency (cost per task) is part of the reported result
notes: Standard-harness verified scores (Standard column; GPT-6 Astra Max also lists 98.6% at $17.3K/task on a Provider Adapter, recorded on the leaderboard separately). BenchLM corroborates the same top three (GPT-6 Astra 62.7%, Claude Opus 5 30.2%, Gemini 3.8 Flash 10.4%, benchlm.ai/benchmarks/arcagi3, Sep 24 2026). New, privately held task set with very high run costs - contamination risk low. GPT-5.6 Sol tops out at 7.8% (Max) and Terra at 0.8% on the official leaderboard.

measures: Cross-benchmark contamination evidence registry and shared-task report; the public report aggregates 566 reported entries over 91 contaminated sources and records evidence contributed by the community.
notes: This is a contamination-evidence resource rather than a capability benchmark. It is included to support contamination checks for the public code/security benchmarks above; no claim is made here that every listed benchmark has a verified CONDA entry.

measures: Audits CyBench traces for answer leakage/cheating and compares ordinary solve rates with clean-pass solve rates under no-anti-cheat, standard, and severe anti-cheat prompts.
notes: This is an evaluation-integrity study rather than a new benchmark. The abstract reports auditing 1,518 traces across 22 models and 23 CyBench challenges and should be read alongside CyBench leaderboard results because harness leakage can inflate scores.

maintainer: gaia-benchmark (Meta-FAIR and collaborators); leaderboard is a Hugging Face Space with server-side scoring
measures: 466 real-world assistant questions across three difficulty levels: multi-step reasoning, web browsing, tool use and multimodal understanding; exact-match scoring against withheld answers
notes: Scores are agent/system setups, not bare models, except GPT-5 Mini (bare-model board). The same benchmark shows very different numbers depending on the harness (rapidclaw documents 74.6% Princeton HAL vs 52.3% BenchLM vs 44.8% bare-model for different leaders), so cross-board comparison is invalid. Humans score around 92%. Test answers are withheld and scoring is server-side - contamination risk low. GAIA is at best a weak proxy for F-02 D-SYN (multi-document synthesis); recorded as POSSIBLE_FUTURE_DIMENSION.

maintainer: Rein et al. (NYU); independent public result pages by Epoch AI and Artificial Analysis
measures: 198 hardest graduate-level physics/chemistry/biology multiple-choice questions, expert-written and verified, designed to be Google-proof; scientific reasoning
notes: Claude Opus 5 93.4% is a Vals AI run displayed by BenchLM. Mistral Medium 3.5 74.8% is an aggregator figure (requesty.ai; benchmarklist.com corroborates 74.8); Mistral's own card publishes no GPQA figure. IntuitionLabs (94.1% for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview) cites the Artificial Analysis leaderboard. Dataset released password-protected with a canary string (Epoch AI page) - contamination risk low, though the top of the leaderboard is clustered within ~1.2 points (BenchLM AA-GPQA page), i.e. nearing saturation. Human baselines: PhD specialists ~65-70%.

measures: Controlled contamination experiments and detection-method evaluation on HumanEval (alongside GSM8K and MATH), comparing output-distribution peakedness with perplexity and Min-k% probability signals.
notes: This is a contamination study, not a replacement coding benchmark. The abstract states that CDD can be at chance under verifiable contamination while probability-based methods perform better when any detector exceeds chance; no HumanEval model score is copied.

maintainer: Scale AI (Scale Labs) together with the Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
measures: 2,500 of the hardest expert-vetted, subject-diverse, multimodal closed-ended academic questions; pass@1 with LLM-graded answers; designed to resist benchmark saturation

scores.model: Claude Opus 5.5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort, Default Fallback)
Claude Fable 5.1 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort, Default Fallback)

notes: BenchLM row (65% for Claude Fable 5.1, Sep 27 2026) covers a different protocol mix than Artificial Analysis; BenchLM explicitly keeps tool-assisted and closed-book HLE runs separate, so the 65% and the AA 59.1% are not directly comparable. Gemini 3.8 Flash 54.9% is a vendor claim (HLE-Verified, Google's announcement table as quoted by third-party coverage). CAIS released an HLE-Rolling fork on Sep 17 2026 that is continually cleaned - the rolling refresh is why contamination stays medium rather than high. Vals.ai reports refusal-fallback effects on HLE-style academic benchmarks for Claude (Opus 5 example), so fallback composition matters when comparing rows.

maintainer: TIGER-Lab (Wang, Ma, Zhang et al., Wenhu Chen); official leaderboard on Hugging Face
measures: Graduate-level multitask knowledge and reasoning: 12,000 questions across 14 domains, 10 answer options, reasoning-heavy; extends/supersedes MMLU
notes: Gemini 3.8 Flash and Claude Opus 5 values are Vals AI runs displayed by BenchLM. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 74.1 is a vendor claim (DeepSeek model card base table, quoted by BenchLM). Successor of MMLU, which is saturated (97-99% frontier, benchlm.ai/blog/posts/mmlu-vs-mmlu-pro); no distinct post-MMLU-Pro successor found in this pass; global variant GMMLU exists (Claude Opus 5 94.3%, llm-stats). Public dataset since 2024 derived from public sources, multiple trackers report nearing saturation - contamination risk high. No A-scope benchmark maps directly to the six F-02 dimensions; knowledge/reasoning dimension is POSSIBLE_FUTURE_DIMENSION.

maintainer: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2; Nouha Dziri and colleagues)
measures: Controlled mathematical-reasoning generalization along three axes (exploratory, compositional, transformative) across six domains, using 40 templated problem generators; also used to study RL (GRPO) effects on generalization
notes: Scores stay unknown: the Ai2 announcement (June 24 2025) names the evaluated models (DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7, OpenAI o3-mini, o4-mini, and GRPO-tuned Qwen2.5-7B variants) but publishes no per-model score table on the accessed page, and no maintained public leaderboard was found in this pass. Templated generation with controlled train/test splits keeps contamination risk low. Status unknown rather than active: no evidence of ongoing maintenance was found. Qualitative findings only: accuracy degrades sharply with problem complexity; ~38% of DeepSeek-R1's incorrect responses initially contained the correct answer before self-correction.
